The original morning report's hypothesis ('probably a macOS permission issue, empty log file') was WRONG and has been corrected with reproducible evidence. Root cause: watchdog.sh calls `tmux send-keys` with no PATH set (neither in the script nor the crontab). cron's default minimal PATH on this Mac is '/usr/gnu/bin:/usr/local/bin:/bin:/usr/bin:.' -- tmux actually lives at /opt/homebrew/bin/tmux (Homebrew on Apple Silicon), which is NOT on that path. Reproduced directly: `env -i HOME=$HOME LOGNAME=$(whoami) /bin/bash -c 'tmux send-keys ...'` fails with 'tmux: command not found', exit code 127. The script's own `2>/dev/null` redirects on every tmux call silently swallowed this error every single time, which is also why /tmp/parisesa-watchdog.log stayed empty (0 bytes, mtime frozen at first creation) even though `log show --predicate process==cron` independently confirms cron itself fired every 5 minutes all night without fail (both the parisesa and pariprashna crontab entries dispatch on schedule, UID resolution succeeds). Verified NO permission/TCC/Accessibility issue exists: cron runs as the same UID (504) as the interactive shell; the tmux socket (/private/tmp/tmux-504/default) is owned by that same UID; `tmux send-keys` uses tmux's own IPC socket, not macOS UI-automation APIs (unlike osascript/System Events), so it was never going to need an Accessibility grant in the first place. With PATH corrected, `tmux list-sessions` successfully reaches the real 'parisesa' session -- confirming PATH truly was the only blocker.
evidence: log show --predicate process==cron --last 24h (many real firings, both crontab jobs, every 5 min); env -i reproduction of the exact 127 failure; socket ownership check (same UID); working tmux call once PATH is corrected.
title: Watchdog root cause conclusively identified: PATH problem, not a permission problem

detail: Design: launchd user agent (com.marsys.parisesa-v4-watchdog, StartInterval=60) replacing cron; kept tmux send-keys (no TCC/Accessibility needed, already proven); CronCreate+/loop stopgap kept as courtesy supplement only -- it cannot substitute for external revival since it requires an already-alive session to self-schedule the next wakeup. Escalated to an Opus-5 design review before install. Opus endorsed launchd over a bare crontab PATH= fix (no-overlap guarantee vs cron stacking runs; separate stdout/stderr closes the swallowed-stderr half of the v1 defect structurally; launchctl kickstart gives a real test trigger) and confirmed the TCC.db 'authorization denied' seen during Step 1a investigation is normal SIP behavior, not a red flag. Opus found 4 real blocking defects in the first draft: (1) unconditional C-c into a live TUI Claude pane is swallowed by the app, not delivered as SIGINT -- fixed by branching on tmux pane_current_command (shell vs resident process); (2) no cooldown -- at 60s StartInterval a stale heartbeat outliving one cycle would re-fire the revival sequence every minute forever, interrupting the very session just launched -- fixed with a cooldown stamp file (600s) + max-attempts cap (3) that writes a WATCHDOG_ALERT.flag instead of retrying silently forever; (3) 1200s stale threshold too tight -- a real subagent in this repo was independently observed running 30+ minutes with no heartbeat write during normal healthy operation -- raised to 2700s; (4) this Mac sleeps after 1 minute idle with only short-lived caffeinate holds observed -- neither cron nor launchd runs during sleep -- documented as a launch-time responsibility (hold caffeinate -dimsu or pmset sleep 0 for the campaign window), not something the watchdog script itself can fix.
evidence: Full Opus-5 review transcript captured in session; watchdog.sh v3 and com.marsys.parisesa-v4-watchdog.plist incorporate all 4 fixes plus the TMUX_TMPDIR pin and set -o pipefail Opus also flagged.
title: Watchdog replacement design: launchd + branch-aware revival, Opus-5 reviewed with 4 blocking fixes applied before install

detail: The FIRST attempt at Step 1c testing (before the isolated-harness redesign) created a plain `tmux new-session` and ran the real watchdog logic against it, believing it to be a blank pane. It was not: `claude --continue`'s session-resume is scoped by the invoking shell's cwd, not by tmux session identity, and the test pane's inherited cwd (/Users/Dev/Vibe-Coding/Apps/Madhav, the shared primary checkout) coincided with the cwd of a live, unrelated PARIPRASHNA campaign conversation (PR #1396 / DD-16/DD-17 close-out, session waiting on CI). The test's `claude --continue` + 'Resume per RESUME.md' sequence was delivered into THAT real session, not a fresh one. It had only completed one read-only search (no writes, no commits, no pushes) before being interrupted with Escape within roughly 90 seconds of the mistaken send; a follow-up correction message was sent explaining the error and asking it to disregard and continue its actual work, which it did cleanly (confirmed: 'Understood, ignoring that -- continuing to wait on PR #1396', then resumed its own CI-wait loop). No file, branch, commit, or PR was touched by the interference. IMPORTANT DESIGN IMPLICATION for the real (non-test) watchdog: `claude --continue` is NOT scoped to a specific campaign/session identity, only to the invoking shell's cwd -- if the real 'parisesa' tmux pane's shell were ever at the wrong cwd when the watchdog fires (e.g., mid-session `cd`, or a shell that respawned in the wrong directory), the exact same hijack could happen for real, silently, with no error surfaced. This was NOT one of the 4 defects the Opus review caught (it wasn't visible until live-tested) and is flagged in the closeout report as a residual risk the owner should weigh, with a suggested mitigation (verify the pane's cwd via `tmux display -p '#{pane_current_path}'` matches the expected conductor path before sending `claude --continue`, abort+alert instead of sending blind if it does not) noted as a candidate hardening item for a future session, NOT implemented in this session (would require another round of testing this session's own boundaries and time did not allow after the correction).

Escalated the v4 cwd-guard patch to Opus 5 before install (same discipline as the closeout session). Opus found the guard was real but incomplete in 4 ways: (1) `*sh` glob also matches ssh/fish/dash/csh -- an ssh'd pane's LOCAL cwd would pass while claude --continue got typed into a REMOTE shell; (2) cwd alone doesn't prove session identity -- live-checked: this exact project directory holds 2 separate conversation histories, --continue resumes whichever has the newer mtime, invisible to a cwd check; (3) tmux display -p on a bad pane index was found (live-tested by Opus) to silently report the ACTIVE pane's info rather than erroring, while send-keys on the same index correctly fails -- the guard could validate a different pane than the one receiving the send; (4) the abort wasn't rate-limited, would re-fire every 60s forever and re-stamp the alert's detected_epoch every time. #1386 (F-69, 4th and final round on one PR): Opus-5's round-3 re-review, WHILE confirming the 5th shape fix, independently found a 6TH leak of its own: mi_darshana.py duplicates the same suppressed float into BOTH provenance_chain.grade AND provenance_chain.propensity for manifestation_grammar rows -- nulling only .grade left the identical number readable via .propensity in the same served row (live-confirmed all 10 manifestation_grammar rows on the canonical chart currently carry this key, latent). Final re-review pending.

Both new call sites (explain.ts, now.ts) could read real kala_gochara_windows rows for any caller-supplied chart_id regardless of entitlement -- confirmed this PR was never merged, so zero live exposure occurred. FIXED: added an explicit remoteAuthorize(principal, chartId) gate at both call sites, matching the tool wrapper's own pattern exactly; mutation-tested (removing the gate makes a new denied-access test fail, proving gochara data was actually served without it); added a real test proving denial produces insufficient_data with computeGocharaForecast never called, not a silent fall-through. Confirmed the reviewer's separately-noted PRE-EXISTING similar gap elsewhere in now.ts (not part of this PR's diff) was correctly left alone as out of scope. 24/24 tests pass; tsc clean. Re-review pending.

#1391 (F-67 bodha_pratijna_get registration): Opus-5 found the new tool's description was copied verbatim from a stale generated file (no CI diff-check gate on that generator) and reintroduced a claim (supporting_signal_ids/contradicting_signal_ids populated) a prior lane deliberately removed since those fields are ALWAYS NULL under the current engine version, plus omitted the real no_evidence status value entirely from what the LLM-facing surface documents. FIXED: sourced the description from the live capability's own text instead of the generated copy; added no_evidence to both the tool description and the status filter param's own describe(). Also wired the test into CI (5th occurrence of the missing-CI-wiring pattern tonight, following #1370/#1383/#1389 and now #1391). 6/6 tests pass; tsc clean. Re-review pending.

detail: The 20:32:44Z Build & Deploy MCP run's post-deploy smoke failure (valid canary bearer key rejected 401) was investigated to completion. Root cause: transient, not a code regression. The IDENTICAL probe (same canary key, same bearer-auth check) against a DIFFERENT deploy just ~9 minutes later (20:41:54Z run) passed cleanly (200). deploy.yml's own MCP bearer-key validation is a cross-service call-through to amjis-web's /api/mcp/keys/validate (auth.ts) -- and the failed run's own job list shows Build & Deploy Web ALSO ran in the same workflow invocation, meaning MCP's smoke-time auth validation likely raced against amjis-web's own concurrent deploy/warm-up window in that specific run. By the next run, web was already stable, and MCP's validation call-through succeeded normally. No code fix applied -- this is an operational/infra characteristic of the pipeline's concurrent multi-service deploy design, not a defect introduced by any PR merged tonight, and the safety net (smoke gate blocking promotion) worked exactly as intended: zero production impact, confirmed via live health check + traffic-split inspection showing the currently-promoted revision is from the run that passed cleanly.
evidence: gh run view --log for both the failed (32414660129) and successful (32415489725) workflow_run-triggered deploys, comparing the identical bearer-auth probe's timestamped output in each. Live gcloud run services describe confirming current 100%-traffic revision matches the successful run.
next_action: none -- logged as a genuine, non-blocking operational finding for the closure report; not pursued further given zero live impact and finite session time better spent on the remaining PR queue
